          "physical_scope": "A specified sequence of finite-state macroscopic models at positive temperature with a declared density, interactions, boundary conditions, and normalization; no limiting existence, ensemble equivalence, or critical singularity is asserted.",
          "inventory_expansion_required": false,
          "statement": "Use $\\mathbb N$ from [[def-natural-numbers]], which includes $0$, and define $\\mathbb N_{>0}:=\\mathbb N\\setminus\\{0\\}$. A **finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract** specifies a sequence $(X_k,E_k,g_k,V_k,n_k)_{k\\in\\mathbb N_{>0}}$, where each $X_k$ is a finite nonempty state set, $E_k:X_k\\to\\mathbb R$ assigns finite energies in joules, $g_k:X_k\\to(0,\\infty)$ assigns positive dimensionless weights, $V_k>0$ is physical volume in $\\mathrm{m^3}$, and, for one declared species, $n_k>0$ is its amount in moles. A fixed-density sequence has $V_k\\to\\infty$ and $n_k/V_k\\to\\rho\\in(0,\\infty)$ in $\\mathrm{mol\\,m^{-3}}$. Boundary conditions, interaction rules, and the choice of a volume or amount normalization are part of the contract and must be held fixed or explicitly tracked as $k$ varies.\n\nFor $T>0$, set $\\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, with $k_B$ and units from [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The finite-state canonical partition sum is\n\n$$\nZ_k(\\beta):=\\sum_{x\\in X_k}g_k(x)e^{-\\beta E_k(x)},\n$$\n\nas the finite case of [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]]. It is a positive finite real number. Define $F_k(\\beta):=-\\beta^{-1}\\log Z_k(\\beta)$ in joules and $f_k(\\beta):=F_k(\\beta)/V_k$ in $\\mathrm{J\\,m^{-3}}$. The specified thermodynamic-limit value is $f(\\beta,\\rho):=\\lim_{k\\to\\infty} f_k(\\beta)$ **if this limit exists**. A limit per mole or per lattice site is a different normalization and must be stated separately.\n\nThis is a contract for what a limit claim must specify, not a theorem that the limit exists. It asserts no uniformity in $\\beta$, derivative interchange, ensemble equivalence, convergence rate, or nonanalyticity. A finite model's regularity and any limiting singularity require their own arguments; neither is inferred from the word “thermodynamic limit.”",

          "physical_scope": "A closed reacting system at fixed positive reservoir temperature and fixed external pressure, represented by a system process record and an admitted isolated-compound extension with the exact ideal-reservoir, pressure-store, and feasible-set data stated here; no external matter exchange, omitted work channel, nonideal reservoir, or kinetic relaxation claim is included.",
          "inventory_expansion_required": true,
          "statement": "Fix a closed system $s$ of constitution $c$, with equilibrium domain $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], and fix $T_0>0$ and $p_0>0$. Define, for $x\\in D_c$,\n$$\n\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x):=U_c(x)+p_0V_c(x)-T_0S_c(x),\n$$\nwhere $U_c,V_c$ are the dimensioned energy and volume maps of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] and $S_c$ is the adopted entropy of [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Thus $\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ has units joules.\n\nLet $P_s\\in\\mathcal P_{\\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ be an admitted closed system process record as defined in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with system endpoints $x_{P_s}^-,x_{P_s}^+\\in D_c$. Let $R$ be its ideal thermal reservoir and $B$ its ideal pressure store; both lie inside a declared isolated-compound outer boundary. Let $\\widehat P$ be an admitted process record for that isolated compound. By an extension, require that $\\widehat P$ has the same time interval, system endpoints, system configuration path, and system-side protocol and transfer records as $P_s$, together with the reservoir and store records. Write its compound endpoint association as\n$$\n\\rho_{\\widehat P}(\\pm)=(x_{P_s}^\\pm,y_R^\\pm,y_B^\\pm)\\in\\mathcal F\\subseteq D_c\\times Y_R\\times Y_B,\n$$\nwhere $Y_R,Y_B$ are the model-declared reservoir and store state sets and $\\mathcal F$ is the exact feasible endpoint set from [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The system protocol assigns heat $Q[P_s]$ and work $W_{\\rm on}[P_s]$ to $P_s$; the auxiliary endpoint changes in $\\widehat P$ satisfy the reservoir and store relations in [A1]–[A2] below. No matter crosses the compound boundary, no work channel other than pressure-store work acts on the system, and no other energy-coordinate changes are omitted.\n\nThen the system endpoint difference obeys\n$$\n\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x_{P_s}^+)-\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x_{P_s}^-)\\le0.\n$$\nIf the final compound endpoint $\\rho_{\\widehat P}(+)$ is an attained global entropy maximum on $\\mathcal F$, then $x_{P_s}^+$ attains a global minimum of $\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ on the system projection\n$$\n\\Pi_s(\\mathcal F):=\\{x\\in D_c:\\exists y_R\\in Y_R,\\ y_B\\in Y_B\\text{ with }(x,y_R,y_B)\\in\\mathcal F\\}.\n$$\nThis is a conditional model deduction; it does not assert that arbitrary fixed-$T,p$ reactions have this preparation or that the system reaches the minimum dynamically.",

          "physical_scope": "Model-specified phase branches of nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic systems in positive-temperature, positive-composition, positive-amount charts; intensive scale invariance and same-tag homogeneity are separate branch assumptions, and no branch existence, stability, boundary smoothness, or universal phase rule is asserted.",
          "inventory_expansion_required": false,
          "statement": "Fix a constitution $c$ with $C\\ge1$ named species and its equilibrium state domain $D_c\\subseteq\\mathbb R^{C+2}$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. An interior composition is represented by\n\n$$\nx=(x_1,\\ldots,x_{C-1})\\in\\Delta_{C-1}^{\\circ}:=\\{x\\in\\mathbb R^{C-1}:x_i>0,\\ \\sum_{i=1}^{C-1}x_i<1\\},\n$$\n\nwith $x_C:=1-\\sum_{i<C}x_i>0$; for $C=1$, $\\mathbb R^0=\\{0\\}$ and $x_1=1$.\n\nA **phase branch** $\\alpha$ is model data consisting of an open chart $W_\\alpha\\subseteq(0,\\infty)\\times\\mathbb R\\times\\Delta_{C-1}^{\\circ}\\times(0,\\infty)$ with coordinates $(T,p,x,m)$ and a $C^1$ diffeomorphism $\\sigma_\\alpha:W_\\alpha\\to U_\\alpha$ onto an open subset $U_\\alpha\\subseteq\\mathbb R^{C+2}$ contained in the equilibrium state domain $D_c$. Here $T$ is in kelvins, $p$ is in pascals, $m$ is total amount in moles, and $C^1$ means continuous first coordinate derivatives as in [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. The chart dimension is $C+2$, matching the ambient dimension of $D_c$. The map $\\sigma_\\alpha$ takes values in numerical state coordinates; its physical SI state map is explicitly $\\chi_\\alpha=\\Phi_c\\circ\\sigma_\\alpha$, where $\\Phi_c$ is the numerical-to-SI unit map of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Thus the physical amounts at this point are $n_j=m x_j$, and the numerical amount coordinates in $\\sigma_\\alpha$ are $n_j/(1\\,\\mathrm{mol})$. Derivative-defined physical state functions are evaluated on $\\chi_\\alpha(T,p,x,m)$, or equivalently pulled back along $\\Phi_c$ to $\\sigma_\\alpha(T,p,x,m)$. At $\\sigma_\\alpha(T,p,x,m)$ in this precise pullback sense, the derivative-defined state functions of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]] give temperature $T$, pressure $p$, and mole fractions $x_j=n_j/m$; here $n_{\\mathrm{tot}}:=\\sum_{i=1}^C n_i=m$ uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]]. An **intensive phase branch** additionally has each derivative-defined chemical potential $\\mu_j(T,p,x,m)$ independent of $m$ throughout $W_\\alpha$; write its value as $\\mu_j^\\alpha(T,p,x)$. This scale invariance is an explicit constitutive model property, not a consequence of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. A valid local response chart and its inverse are as in [[def-td-response-functions]] and [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. Existence of $W_\\alpha$ or $\\sigma_\\alpha$ is a model premise, not a consequence of the equations of thermodynamics.\n\nOn a branch with a valid natural-variable chart, $G^\\alpha$ denotes the Gibbs potential of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]] restricted to the branch. For a one-component branch with amount $m_\\alpha>0$, define $g_\\alpha:=G^\\alpha/m_\\alpha$, $s_\\alpha:=S_\\alpha/m_\\alpha$, and $v_\\alpha:=V_\\alpha/m_\\alpha$, in $\\mathrm{J\\,mol^{-1}}$, $\\mathrm{J\\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\\mathrm{m^3\\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively. These quotients need not be independent of amount, and $g_\\alpha=\\mu^\\alpha$ is not assumed by this definition. Such an equality requires a separate same-tag homogeneity hypothesis on the branch.\n\nA **phase mixture** of a finite list of branches is a feasible separated compound whose positive phase amounts $m_\\alpha$ have fractions $\\lambda_\\alpha:=m_\\alpha/\\sum_\\beta m_\\beta>0$ with $\\sum_\\alpha\\lambda_\\alpha=1$. Its extensive coordinates and entropy are those supplied by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] and [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The mixture is in **coexistence** when it is an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint under the declared totals and permitted exchanges, as in [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]. This definition does not assert that a maximum exists, that all branches can exchange every coordinate, or that metastable states are global equilibria.\n\nThe bulk scaling postulate may send a material tag $c$ to a different tag $c^{(\\lambda)}$. It therefore does not supply same-tag degree-one homogeneity of $G^\\alpha$ or $U^\\alpha$ on a phase branch. Any result using $g_\\alpha=\\mu^\\alpha$ must state that additional hypothesis.",

          "physical_scope": "Finite coexisting phase branches in positive-temperature C2 charts at an attained global entropy maximum, and only the energy, volume, or species transfers declared pairwise feasible in both directions.",

          "statement": "Let $P\\ge1$ named phase branches of the same finite species list occupy a separated compound at an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint with the fixed totals and exact feasible set declared by [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] and [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. Assume each phase lies in an open C2 single-phase chart with finite positive temperature. For every pair of phases, assume the following about the feasible set at this endpoint: each named exchange channel permits a sufficiently small nonzero amount of transfer in both directions, while all other state coordinates may be held fixed.\n\nThen, for every pair $\\alpha,\\beta$:\n- if energy exchange is permitted, $T_\\alpha=T_\\beta$;\n- if volume exchange is permitted, $p_\\alpha/T_\\alpha=p_\\beta/T_\\beta$, and if energy exchange is also permitted then $p_\\alpha=p_\\beta$;\n- if species $j$ is transferable, $\\mu_{\\alpha,j}/T_\\alpha=\\mu_{\\beta,j}/T_\\beta$, and if energy exchange is also permitted then $\\mu_{\\alpha,j}=\\mu_{\\beta,j}$.\n\nThe pressure and chemical potentials are the derivative-defined state functions of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. The theorem makes no equality claim for a retained coordinate, a one-sided boundary exchange, or a channel absent from the declared feasible set. It is a model deduction, not evidence that these phases or exchange channels occur in nature.",

          "physical_scope": "Local C1 constrained Gibbs-potential charts for a declared internal reaction network at fixed positive reservoir temperature and pressure; interior conclusions use the admitted process-record model, while boundary conclusions require the explicit boundary-inclusive entropy and auxiliary extension stated here.",
          "inventory_expansion_required": false,
          "statement": "Fix $C\\ge1$ species and $R\\ge1$ declared internal reaction extents. Let $\\nu\\in\\mathbb R^{C\\times R}$ be the dimensionless stoichiometric matrix, let $n^0\\in[0,\\infty)^C$ have units mol, and let $\\xi\\in\\mathbb R^R$ have units mol. The amount vector is $n(\\xi)=n^0+\\nu\\xi$, and the nonnegative-amount feasible extent set is\n$$\n\\mathcal F_\\nu:=\\{\\xi\\in\\mathbb R^R:n^0+\\nu\\xi\\in[0,\\infty)^C\\}.\n$$\nAssume the exact local reaction-feasible extent set is $\\mathcal F_\\nu\\cap U$; no additional local constraint removes any direction in its tangent cone.\nFix $T_0>0$ and $p_0>0$ in a declared natural-variable chart. On an open neighborhood $U$ of a candidate endpoint $\\xi_*$, let $\\Phi:U\\to\\mathbb R$ be a finite $C^1$ constrained Gibbs-potential extension, in joules, satisfying\n$$\nD\\Phi(\\xi)[h]=\\sum_{j=1}^C\\mu_j(\\xi)(\\nu h)_j=(\\nu^{\\mathsf T}\\mu(\\xi))\\cdot h,\n$$\nwhere every $\\mu_j$ is in $\\mathrm{J\\,mol^{-1}}$. At positive amounts, require $\\Phi(\\xi)=U_c(x(\\xi))+p_0V_c(x(\\xi))-T_0S_c(x(\\xi))$ for the system state $x(\\xi)$, with $U_c,V_c,S_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] and [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]; its derivative is that of the local Gibbs chart supplied by [[def-td-legendre-potentials]] and [[pthm-td-potential-differentials]].\n\nIf all amounts at $\\xi_*$ are positive, assume $\\xi_*$ is the system endpoint of a closed system process record and its admitted isolated-compound extension exactly as in [[pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-minimum]], is a global entropy-maximizing endpoint on that extension's exact feasible set, and the record's system projection contains every state $x(\\xi)$ for $\\xi\\in\\mathcal F_\\nu\\cap U$. If at least one amount is zero, it is outside [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]; in that boundary case, assume instead that the model supplies a boundary-inclusive state domain with finite $C^1$ maps $\\bar U_c,\\bar V_c,\\bar S_c:U\\to\\mathbb R$ in joules, $\\mathrm{m^3}$, and $\\mathrm{J\\,K^{-1}}$, respectively, that $\\Phi(\\xi)=\\bar U_c(\\xi)+p_0\\bar V_c(\\xi)-T_0\\bar S_c(\\xi)$, and that its exact isolated-compound model has fixed total energy, an ideal reservoir with $S_R(E_R)=S_{R,0}+E_R/T_0$, a constant-entropy pressure store satisfying $E_B-p_0\\bar V_c(\\xi)=C_B$, and a feasible-set projection equal to $\\mathcal F_\\nu\\cap U$. Assume $\\xi_*$ is an attained global entropy maximum on that boundary-inclusive set. This additional boundary model premise is not supplied by the positive-mole state chart or by [[pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-minimum]].\n\nUnder the relevant interior or boundary assumptions above, $\\xi_*$ locally minimizes $\\Phi$ on $\\mathcal F_\\nu\\cap U$. Let $J_*:=\\{j:n^0_j+(\\nu\\xi_*)_j=0\\}$ be the active species set. Then the first-order necessary condition is\n$$\n(\\nu^{\\mathsf T}\\mu(\\xi_*))\\cdot h\\ge0\\qquad\\text{for every }h\\in T_{\\mathcal F_\\nu}(\\xi_*),\n$$\nwhere\n$$\nT_{\\mathcal F_\\nu}(\\xi_*):=\\{h\\in\\mathbb R^R:(\\nu h)_j\\ge0\\text{ for every }j\\in J_*\\}.\n$$\nIf $\\xi_*$ is interior to $\\mathcal F_\\nu$, this reduces to $\\nu^{\\mathsf T}\\mu(\\xi_*)=0$. {
      "id": "td-phases-and-limits",
      "title": "Phases And Limits",
      "category": "thermodynamics",
      "library": "physics",
      "companion": "td-phases-and-limits-examples",
      "kind": "A",
      "requires": [
        "td-math-mixture-dynamics-and-shells",

      ],
      "items": [
        {
          "id": "def-td-thermodynamic-limit-contract",
          "kind": "definition",
          "domain": "physics",
          "title": "Finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract",
          "reference": "items/def-td-thermodynamic-limit-contract.md",
          "design_state": "Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.",
          "dependency_level": 3,
          "deps": [
            "def-td-equilibrium-state-domain",
            "def-td-si-quantities",
            "def-natural-numbers",
            "def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model"
          ],
          "dependency_roles": {
            "def-td-equilibrium-state-domain": "formulation-prerequisite",
            "def-td-si-quantities": "formulation-prerequisite",
            "def-natural-numbers": "mathematical-premise",
            "def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model": "mathematical-premise"
          },
          "physical_scope": "A specified sequence of finite-state macroscopic models at positive temperature with a declared density, interactions, boundary conditions, and normalization; no limiting existence, ensemble equivalence, or critical singularity is asserted.",
          "inventory_expansion_required": false,
          "statement": "Use $\\mathbb N$ from [[def-natural-numbers]], which includes $0$, and define $\\mathbb N_{>0}:=\\mathbb N\\setminus\\{0\\}$. A **finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract** specifies a sequence $(X_k,E_k,g_k,V_k,n_k)_{k\\in\\mathbb N_{>0}}$, where each $X_k$ is a finite nonempty state set, $E_k:X_k\\to\\mathbb R$ assigns finite energies in joules, $g_k:X_k\\to(0,\\infty)$ assigns positive dimensionless weights, $V_k>0$ is physical volume in $\\mathrm{m^3}$, and, for one declared species, $n_k>0$ is its amount in moles. A fixed-density sequence has $V_k\\to\\infty$ and $n_k/V_k\\to\\rho\\in(0,\\infty)$ in $\\mathrm{mol\\,m^{-3}}$. Boundary conditions, interaction rules, and the choice of a volume or amount normalization are part of the contract and must be held fixed or explicitly tracked as $k$ varies.\n\nFor $T>0$, set $\\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, with $k_B$ and units from [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The finite-state canonical partition sum is\n\n$$\nZ_k(\\beta):=\\sum_{x\\in X_k}g_k(x)e^{-\\beta E_k(x)},\n$$\n\nas the finite case of [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]]. It is a positive finite real number. Define $F_k(\\beta):=-\\beta^{-1}\\log Z_k(\\beta)$ in joules and $f_k(\\beta):=F_k(\\beta)/V_k$ in $\\mathrm{J\\,m^{-3}}$. The specified thermodynamic-limit value is $f(\\beta,\\rho):=\\lim_{k\\to\\infty} f_k(\\beta)$ **if this limit exists**. A limit per mole or per lattice site is a different normalization and must be stated separately.\n\nThis is a contract for what a limit claim must specify, not a theorem that the limit exists. It asserts no uniformity in $\\beta$, derivative interchange, ensemble equivalence, convergence rate, or nonanalyticity. A finite model's regularity and any limiting singularity require their own arguments; neither is inferred from the word “thermodynamic limit.”",
          "provenance": {
            "statement": "ai-altered",
            "proof": "not-applicable"
          },
          "sources": {
            "references": [
              {
                "title": "David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, Chapter 5, §5.4.3",
                "url": "https://davidtong.org/teaching/statistical-physics/statmechhtml/S5"
              },
              {
                "title": "Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §§4.1–4.2",
                "url": "https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Thermodynamics_and_Statistical_Mechanics/Essential_Graduate_Physics_-_Statistical_Mechanics_%28Likharev%29/04%3A_Phase_Transitions/4.01%3A_First_order_phase_transitions"
              }
            ]
          },
          "library": "physics"
        },
        {
          "id": "pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-minimum",
          "kind": "physics-theorem",

          "title": "Fixed-temperature and fixed-pressure potential minimum with internal reactions",

      "items": [
        {
          "id": "def-td-thermodynamic-limit-contract",
          "kind": "definition",
          "domain": "physics",
          "title": "Finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract",
          "reference": "items/def-td-thermodynamic-limit-contract.md",
          "design_state": "Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.",
          "dependency_level": 0,
          "deps": [
            "def-td-equilibrium-state-domain",
            "def-td-si-quantities",
            "def-natural-numbers",
            "def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model"
          ],
          "dependency_roles": {
            "def-td-equilibrium-state-domain": "formulation-prerequisite",
            "def-td-si-quantities": "formulation-prerequisite",
            "def-natural-numbers": "mathematical-premise",
            "def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model": "mathematical-premise"
          },
          "physical_scope": "A specified sequence of finite-state macroscopic models at positive temperature with a declared density, interactions, boundary conditions, and normalization; no limiting existence, ensemble equivalence, or critical singularity is asserted.",
          "inventory_expansion_required": false,
          "statement": "Use $\\mathbb N$ from *The natural numbers $\\mathbb{N}$ (von Neumann)*, which includes $0$, and define $\\mathbb N_{>0}:=\\mathbb N\\setminus\\{0\\}$. A **finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract** specifies a sequence $(X_k,E_k,g_k,V_k,n_k)_{k\\in\\mathbb N_{>0}}$, where each $X_k$ is a finite nonempty state set, $E_k:X_k\\to\\mathbb R$ assigns finite energies in joules, $g_k:X_k\\to(0,\\infty)$ assigns positive dimensionless weights, $V_k>0$ is physical volume in $\\mathrm{m^3}$, and, for one declared species, $n_k>0$ is its amount in moles. A fixed-density sequence has $V_k\\to\\infty$ and $n_k/V_k\\to\\rho\\in(0,\\infty)$ in $\\mathrm{mol\\,m^{-3}}$. Boundary conditions, interaction rules, and the choice of a volume or amount normalization are part of the contract and must be held fixed or explicitly tracked as $k$ varies.\n\nFor $T>0$, set $\\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, with $k_B$ and units from *SI quantities and unit conventions*. The finite-state canonical partition sum is\n\n$$\nZ_k(\\beta):=\\sum_{x\\in X_k}g_k(x)e^{-\\beta E_k(x)},\n$$\n\nas the finite case of *Countable canonical model*. It is a positive finite real number. Define $F_k(\\beta):=-\\beta^{-1}\\log Z_k(\\beta)$ in joules and $f_k(\\beta):=F_k(\\beta)/V_k$ in $\\mathrm{J\\,m^{-3}}$. The specified thermodynamic-limit value is $f(\\beta,\\rho):=\\lim_{k\\to\\infty} f_k(\\beta)$ **if this limit exists**. A limit per mole or per lattice site is a different normalization and must be stated separately.\n\nThis is a contract for what a limit claim must specify, not a theorem that the limit exists. It asserts no uniformity in $\\beta$, derivative interchange, ensemble equivalence, convergence rate, or nonanalyticity. A finite model's regularity and any limiting singularity require their own arguments; neither is inferred from the word “thermodynamic limit.”",
          "provenance": {
            "statement": "ai-altered",
            "proof": "not-applicable"
          },
          "sources": {
            "references": [
              {
                "title": "David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, Chapter 5, §5.4.3",
                "url": "https://davidtong.org/teaching/statistical-physics/statmechhtml/S5"
              },
              {
                "title": "Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §§4.1–4.2",
                "url": "https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Thermodynamics_and_Statistical_Mechanics/Essential_Graduate_Physics_-_Statistical_Mechanics_%28Likharev%29/04%3A_Phase_Transitions/4.01%3A_First_order_phase_transitions"
              }
            ]
          },
          "library": "physics"
        },
        {
          "id": "pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-minimum",
          "kind": "physics-theorem",
          "domain": "physics",
          "title": "Fixed-temperature and fixed-pressure potential minimum with internal reactions",
          "reference": "items/pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-minimum.md",
          "design_state": "Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.",
          "dependency_level": 0,
          "deps": [
            "def-td-equilibrium-state-domain",
            "def-td-si-quantities",
            "def-td-process-and-protocol",
            "def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set",
            "post-td-bulk-additivity",
            "post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy",
            "post-td-first-law-energy",
            "post-td-macroscopic-second-law",
            "post-td-entropy-maximum"
          ],
          "dependency_roles": {
            "def-td-equilibrium-state-domain": "formulation-prerequisite",
            "def-td-si-quantities": "formulation-prerequisite",
            "def-td-process-and-protocol": "formulation-prerequisite",
            "def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set": "formulation-prerequisite",
            "post-td-bulk-additivity": "physical-assumption",
            "post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy": "physical-assumption",
            "post-td-first-law-energy": "physical-assumption",
            "post-td-macroscopic-second-law": "physical-assumption",
            "post-td-entropy-maximum": "physical-assumption"
          },
          "physical_scope": "A closed reacting system at fixed positive reservoir temperature and fixed external pressure, represented by a system process record and an admitted isolated-compound extension with the exact ideal-reservoir, pressure-store, and feasible-set data stated here; no external matter exchange, omitted work channel, nonideal reservoir, or kinetic relaxation claim is included.",
          "inventory_expansion_required": true,
          "statement": "Fix a closed system $s$ of constitution $c$, with equilibrium domain $D_c$ from *Equilibrium state domains*, and fix $T_0>0$ and $p_0>0$. Define, for $x\\in D_c$,\n$$\n\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x):=U_c(x)+p_0V_c(x)-T_0S_c(x),\n$$\nwhere $U_c,V_c$ are the dimensioned energy and volume maps of *Equilibrium state domains* and $S_c$ is the adopted entropy of *Concave macroscopic fundamental entropy*. Thus $\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ has units joules.\n\nLet $P_s\\in\\mathcal P_{\\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ be an admitted closed system process record as defined in *Thermodynamic process records and transfer conventions*, with system endpoints $x_{P_s}^-,x_{P_s}^+\\in D_c$. Let $R$ be its ideal thermal reservoir and $B$ its ideal pressure store; both lie inside a declared isolated-compound outer boundary. Let $\\widehat P\\in\\mathcal P_{\\mathrm{cl}}(s\\sqcup R\\sqcup B)$ be an admitted core closed process record for that isolated compound, whose supplied total mass is positive, whose endpoint center-of-mass velocities are defined in one fixed Galilean chart, and whose compound center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change. These are conditions on the whole compound, additional to the system-record conditions. By an extension, require that $\\widehat P$ has the same time interval, system endpoints, system configuration path, and system-side protocol and transfer records as $P_s$, together with the reservoir and store records. Write its compound endpoint association as\n$$\n\\rho_{\\widehat P}(\\pm)=(x_{P_s}^\\pm,y_R^\\pm,y_B^\\pm)\\in\\mathcal F\\subseteq D_c\\times Y_R\\times Y_B,\n$$\nwhere $Y_R,Y_B$ are the model-declared reservoir and store equilibrium state sets, represented as admitted constituent state domains (or subsets thereof) in the second-law endpoint split; $E_R,E_B$ and their entropies are the corresponding dimensioned state maps. The split is admitted as independent separated macroscopic systems by *Concave macroscopic fundamental entropy*. The set $\\mathcal F$ is the exact feasible endpoint set from *Isolated compound and feasible equilibrium set*. The system protocol assigns heat $Q[P_s]$ and work $W_{\\rm on}[P_s]$ to $P_s$; the auxiliary endpoint changes in $\\widehat P$ satisfy the reservoir and store relations in [A1]–[A2] below. No matter crosses the compound boundary, no work channel other than pressure-store work acts on the system, and no other energy-coordinate changes are omitted.\n\nThen the system endpoint difference obeys\n$$\n\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x_{P_s}^+)-\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x_{P_s}^-)\\le0.\n$$\nIf the final compound endpoint $\\rho_{\\widehat P}(+)$ is an attained global entropy maximum on $\\mathcal F$, then $x_{P_s}^+$ attains a global minimum of $\\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ on the system projection\n$$\n\\Pi_s(\\mathcal F):=\\{x\\in D_c:\\exists y_R\\in Y_R,\\ y_B\\in Y_B\\text{ with }(x,y_R,y_B)\\in\\mathcal F\\}.\n$$\nThis is a conditional model deduction; it does not assert that arbitrary fixed-$T,p$ reactions have this preparation or that the system reaches the minimum dynamically.",

          "statement": "Let $d\\ge1$ and let $K\\subseteq\\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty compact set of dimensionless generator coordinates.           "title": "Finite-energy PEC and impedance boundary formulation",
          "statement": "Let $I\\subseteq\\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and let $\\Omega\\subseteq\\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded Lipschitz polyhedron in the laboratory frame. Its boundary $\\Gamma=\\partial\\Omega$ has the outward unit normal $n$ on the relative interior of each planar face; edge and vertex values will be irrelevant under the face-area convention below. Use the SI conventions of this framework. In particular $E$ has units $\\mathrm{V\\,m^{-1}}$, $H$ has units $\\mathrm{A\\,m^{-1}}$, $D$ has units $\\mathrm{C\\,m^{-2}}$, $B$ has units $\\mathrm T$, and a volume current density $J$ has units $\\mathrm{A\\,m^{-2}}$.\n\nFor the boundary integrals, let $\\mathcal F$ be the finite family of relative interiors of the planar two-dimensional faces of $\\Gamma$. Write $\\lambda_2$ for Lebesgue measure on $\\mathbb R^2$, defined as the restriction of Lebesgue outer measure to its Carath\\'eodory-measurable sets; under the assumed $\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$, this is a complete measure. For each face $F\\in\\mathcal F$, let $P_F$ be its supporting plane and fix a Euclidean isometry $\\iota_F:\\mathbb R^2\\to P_F$. For every Borel set $A\\subseteq\\Gamma$ (a set in the sigma-algebra generated by the open subsets of $\\Gamma$), define $dS_F(A):=\\lambda_2\\bigl(\\iota_F^{-1}(A\\cap F)\\bigr)$. Any two choices of $\\iota_F$ differ by an affine Euclidean isometry of $\\mathbb R^2$ with absolute Jacobian determinant $1$, so the Borel change-of-variables formula makes $dS_F$ independent of that choice. Each face is bounded and lies in a finite rectangle in its plane, so $dS_F(F)<\\infty$. Set $dS:=\\sum_{F\\in\\mathcal F}dS_F$ on $\\Gamma$. The edges and vertices have $dS$-measure zero and are omitted, so $n$ is the outward face normal $dS$-almost everywhere; its values on edges and vertices do not affect any boundary expression. Since $dS$ is finite and Lebesgue measure restricted to $I$ is sigma-finite, $dS\\otimes d\\lambda_1|_I$ is the unique sigma-finite product measure on $\\Gamma\\times I$, with rectangle values $dS(A)\\lambda_1(J)$ for Borel $A\\subseteq\\Gamma$ and Lebesgue-measurable $J\\subseteq I$. All boundary $L^p(\\Gamma)$ and $L^p(\\Gamma\\times I)$ spaces and almost-everywhere statements use these measures.\n\nEvery cross product in the boundary formulas is the right-handed Euclidean cross product in the positively oriented orthonormal frame basis: for $u=(u_1,u_2,u_3)$ and $v=(v_1,v_2,v_3)$, $u\\times v=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\\,u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\\,u_1v_2-u_2v_1)$, as in the cross-product definition of this library.\n\nFor a real vector field $u\\in L^2(\\Omega;\\mathbb R^3)$, its distributional curl is the distribution defined by\n\n$$\\langle\\operatorname{curl}u,\\varphi\\rangle=\\int_\\Omega u\\cdot\\operatorname{curl}\\varphi\\,d\\lambda_3,\\qquad \\varphi\\in C_c^\\infty(\\Omega;\\mathbb R^3).$$\n\nAs in the real graph space definition of the imported mathematical library, $H(\\operatorname{curl};\\Omega)$ consists of the $L^2$ vector fields whose distributional curl is represented by an $L^2$ vector field, with norm\n\n$$\\|u\\|_{H(\\operatorname{curl};\\Omega)}^2=\\|u\\|_{L^2(\\Omega)}^2+\\|\\operatorname{curl}u\\|_{L^2(\\Omega)}^2.$$\n\nAssume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$ as carried by that imported weak-derivative convention. Let $\\varepsilon,\\mu:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R^{3\\times3}$ be measurable, essentially bounded, real symmetric coefficient fields, independent of time. Require constants $0<a_\\varepsilon\\le b_\\varepsilon<\\infty$ and $0<a_\\mu\\le b_\\mu<\\infty$ such that, for almost every $x\\in\\Omega$ and every $v\\in\\mathbb R^3$,\n\n$$a_\\varepsilon |v|^2\\le v\\cdot\\varepsilon(x)v\\le b_\\varepsilon |v|^2,\\qquad a_\\mu |v|^2\\le v\\cdot\\mu(x)v\\le b_\\mu |v|^2.$$\n\nThe coefficient units are $\\mathrm{F\\,m^{-1}}$ and $\\mathrm{H\\,m^{-1}}$, respectively. At each point $\\overline g$ is a symmetric bilinear form on the tangent space, its components extend smoothly in every boundary chart, and its pointwise inertia is $(3,1,0)$ in the convention of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]. The vector field $\\overline N$ likewise has components that extend smoothly in every boundary chart; it satisfies $\\overline g(\\overline N,\\overline N)<0$ everywhere and $\\overline g(\\overline N,j_*N)<0$ on the interior. The map $j:M\\to\\overline M^\\circ$ is a diffeomorphism onto the interior. The function $\\Omega:\\overline M\\to\\mathbb R$ is smooth in the boundary-chart sense, positive on $j(M)$, and zero with nonzero differential on the designated smooth three-dimensional boundary subset $\\mathscr I^+\\subseteq\\partial\\overline M$. On $j(M)$ the metric satisfies $\\overline g|_{j(M)}=\\Omega^2(j^{-1})^*g$, where pullback is as in [[def-pullback-of-a-covariant-tensor-field]]. The restriction of $\\overline g$ to $T\\mathscr I^+$ has a one-dimensional kernel at every point; this null line is the generator direction, and its future ray is the one whose vectors $v$ satisfy $\\overline g(v,\\overline N)<0$. Thus the designated boundary is null and future-oriented; no completeness of its generators is assumed.\n\nA curve $\\gamma:[0,1]\\to\\overline M$ is **locally absolutely continuous** when it is continuous and, around each parameter value, its coordinate functions in a boundary or interior chart are absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of that chart neighborhood, in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]. Boundary charts take values in relatively open subsets of the closed half-space. To compare two charts around a parameter value, shrink its parameter neighborhood so the coordinate image lies in a compact convex subset of a local-extension domain of the transition map. Its derivative is bounded there, so the mean-value estimate ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]) makes the transition Lipschitz. Applying that bound to the finite disjoint-interval condition for absolute continuity shows that the transformed coordinate functions remain absolutely continuous; the argument in both directions proves chart independence.           "physical_scope": "A Fourier-mode calculation for the exact periodic scalar recurrence only. It gives no convergence theorem for Einstein evolution, no general nonlinear stability result, and no uniform-in-time displacement bound for a nonzero mean velocity.",
          "statement": "Let $N\\ge3$, $h=2\\pi/N$, $k>0$, and $\\lambda=k/h$. Complexify the real\nlinear recurrence of the periodic wave algorithm. For each discrete Fourier\nindex $\\ell\\in\\{0,1,\\ldots,N-1\\}$ define the mode\n$$\ne_\\ell(j):=\\exp(2\\pi i\\ell j/N),\\qquad j\\in\\mathbb Z/N\\mathbb Z.\n$$\nIf $0<\\lambda<1$, every nonconstant mode ($\\ell\\ne0$) has recurrence\ncoefficient\n$$\nc_\\ell:=1-2\\lambda^2\\sin^2(\\pi\\ell/N)\\in(-1,1)\n$$\nand two distinct amplification roots\n$$\nz_{\\ell,\\pm}:=c_\\ell\\pm i\\sqrt{1-c_\\ell^2},\\qquad |z_{\\ell,\\pm}|=1.\n$$\nConsequently, each fixed nonconstant mode has bounded amplitude on every\nfinite slab. For arbitrary real initial arrays define their spatial means by\n$$\n\\bar u^0:=\\frac1N\\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}u^0_j,\\qquad \\bar v^0:=\\frac1N\\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}v^0_j.\n$$\nThe constant mode has the repeated root $1$ and evolves exactly as\n$\\bar u^0+nk\\bar v^0$; for any fixed $T\\ge0$ it is bounded on the slab\n$0\\le nk\\le T$ but has no uniform-in-time displacement bound when\n$\\bar v^0\\ne0$. This statement\ndoes not assert that the condition $0<\\lambda<1$ alone proves convergence of a\nnumerical relativity scheme. Define the nonzero discrete frequencies $\\omega_\\ell:=2h^{-1}|\\sin(\\pi\\ell/N)|$, $1\\le\\ell<N$. On this fixed torus they satisfy the mesh-independent lower bound\n$$\\omega_\\ell\\ge\\frac2\\pi\\qquad(N\\ge3,\\ 1\\le\\ell<N).$$\nIn particular each fixed grid has a positive minimum. This frequency bound is not a mesh-independent amplitude bound for arbitrary unscaled two-step data $(a_0,a_1)$: the distinct-root coefficients in the mode solution can depend on the grid and the initial data. The constant-mode qualifications above are unchanged.\nFor even $N$, the alternating mode with Fourier index $\\ell=N/2$ is called\nthe Nyquist mode. At the endpoint $\\lambda=1$, if $N$ is even and\n$u_j^0=a_0(-1)^j$, $v_j^0=\\beta_0(-1)^j$ for real amplitudes $a_0,\\beta_0$,\nthen each output level satisfies\n$$\nu_j^n=(-1)^j(-1)^n(a_0-nk\\beta_0).\n$$\nThe Nyquist amplification root is repeated at $-1$, and a nonzero Nyquist\nvelocity amplitude $\\beta_0$ gives linear growth in the step number.\n\n",

Thus the scalar residual below\nhas units $\\mathrm m^{-2}$ and its covector components in this angular basis\nhave units $\\mathrm m^{-1}$.\n\nLet $\\mathbb R^{G_{\\boldsymbol\\Delta}}$ denote the real arrays indexed by\nthe grid.           "physical_scope": "A mathematical aliasing example for the discrete constraint diagnostic. It is not a reported simulation, a measurement, or a claim that the sampled data admit a spacetime development.",
          "statement": "Let $N\\ge4$ be even, let $N_2,N_3\\ge3$, let $L_*>0$ be a length, and choose\n$0<\\varepsilon<1$. On $\\mathbb T^3_{2\\pi}$ with dimensionless angular\ncoordinates $x^i$, set\n$$\n\\widetilde h=L_*^2\\bigl((dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2\\bigr),\\qquad \\widetilde\\sigma=0,\\qquad \\tau=0,\\qquad \\phi_N(x)=1+\\varepsilon\\sin(Nx^1/2).\n$$\nTake the vacuum branch with $\\Lambda=0$ and $\\rho=j=0$. Fix any\n$\\kappa>0$ with the SI units specified by the discrete diagnostic; its value\ndrops out because $j=0$. The conformal data are\n$h=\\phi_N^4\\widetilde h$ and $K=0$. Use a periodic mesh with\n$N_1=N$ and counts $N_2,N_3$ in the other directions. Put\n$\\Delta_i=2\\pi/N_i$ and use nodes\n$x^i_{j_i}=2\\pi j_i/N_i$, $0\\le j_i<N_i$, with indices wrapped modulo each\n$N_i$. For $i=1,2,3$, let $\\mathbf e_i$ be the $i$th standard basis vector of\n$\\mathbb Z^3$. For a scalar grid array\n$f_{\\mathbf j}$, use the centered periodic maps\n$$\n(\\delta_i f)_{\\mathbf j}:= \\frac{f_{\\mathbf j+\\mathbf e_i}-f_{\\mathbf j-\\mathbf e_i}}{2\\Delta_i}, \\qquad i=1,2,3,\n$$\nwith indices reduced modulo $(N_1,N_2,N_3)$, and apply them componentwise.\nFor reconstruction, partition each periodic coordinate circle into the\nhalf-open cells\n$$\nC_{\\mathbf j}:=\\prod_{i=1}^3 \\left[\\frac{2\\pi(j_i-1/2)}{N_i}, \\frac{2\\pi(j_i+1/2)}{N_i}\\right)\\pmod{2\\pi},\n$$\nand assign every component on $C_{\\mathbf j}$ its value at node\n$\\mathbf j$. This specifies the piecewise-constant map\n$\\mathcal I_{\\boldsymbol\\Delta}$ in the constraint-residual definition.\nFor the reported residual arrays use uniform dimensionless weights\n$w_{\\mathbf j}:=(NN_2N_3)^{-1}$ and the norm\n$$\n\\| (\\mathcal H_{\\boldsymbol\\Delta},\\mathcal M_{\\boldsymbol\\Delta})\\|_{\\boldsymbol\\Delta,2} :=\\left(\\sum_{\\mathbf j}w_{\\mathbf j} \\left(|\\mathcal H_{\\boldsymbol\\Delta}(\\mathbf j)|^2+ h^{ik}(\\mathbf j)\\mathcal M_{\\boldsymbol\\Delta,i}(\\mathbf j) \\mathcal M_{\\boldsymbol\\Delta,k}(\\mathbf j)\\right)\\right)^{1/2}.\n$$\nThe bars around the scalar residual denote the real absolute value.           "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\\ge1$, $0<\\epsilon\\le1$, and $V\\in C^\\infty(\\mathbb R^d;\\mathbb R)$ with every partial derivative of total order at least $2$ bounded. Set\n$$ h(x,\\xi)=\\frac{|\\xi|^2}{2}+V(x),\\qquad H_\\epsilon^0=-\\frac{\\epsilon^2}{2}\\Delta+V(x)\\quad\\text{on }\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^d). $$\nAssume, as an explicit operator hypothesis, that for each $\\epsilon$ a densely defined self-adjoint operator $H_\\epsilon$ on $L^2(\\mathbb R^d)$ extends $H_\\epsilon^0$ and $\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^d)$ is a core for $H_\\epsilon$. Let $U_\\epsilon(t)$, $t\\in\\mathbb R$, be the strongly continuous unitary group with $U_\\epsilon(0)=I$, preserving $D(H_\\epsilon)$ and satisfying\n$$ i\\,\\partial_tU_\\epsilon(t)y=\\epsilon^{-1}H_\\epsilon U_\\epsilon(t)y\\qquad(y\\in D(H_\\epsilon)). $$\nThus its generator is $-iH_\\epsilon/\\epsilon$; for $t<0$, $U_\\epsilon(t)=U_\\epsilon(-t)^*$. Define the global Hamiltonian flow by\n$$ \\dot x=\\xi,\\qquad \\dot\\xi=-\\nabla V(x),\\qquad \\Phi_0=I. $$\nFor every $a\\in C_c^\\infty(\\mathbb R^{2d})$ and finite $T>0$, there is $C_{T,V,a}<\\infty$, independent of $0<\\epsilon\\le1$, such that\n$$ \\sup_{|t|\\le T} \\left\\|U_\\epsilon(t)^*\\operatorname{Op}^W_\\epsilon(a)U_\\epsilon(t) -\\operatorname{Op}^W_\\epsilon(a\\circ\\Phi_t)\\right\\|_{L^2\\to L^2} \\le C_{T,V,a}\\epsilon^2. $$\nOnly fixed finite times are covered by the first estimate. No Ehrenfest-time, caustic-uniformity, or physical measurement conclusion is asserted. If $V$ is a polynomial of degree at most two, the difference in that branch is identically zero.\n\nThere is also an exact statement for every real quadratic phase-space Hamiltonian. Let $z=(x,\\xi)\\in\\mathbb R^{2d}$, let $G=G^T\\in\\mathbb R^{2d\\times2d}$, $\\ell\\in\\mathbb R^{2d}$ and $c\\in\\mathbb R$, and put\n$$ h(z)=\\tfrac12 z^TGz+\\ell\\cdot z+c. $$\nSet $J=\\begin{pmatrix}0&I_d\\\\-I_d&0\\end{pmatrix}$ and $\\widehat z=(Q_1,\\ldots,Q_d,P_1,\\ldots,P_d)$, where $Q_j u=x_j u$ and $P_j u=-i\\epsilon\\partial_{x_j}u$ on $\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^d)$. On $\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^d)$ define the Weyl realization by\n$$ H_{\\epsilon,h}^0:=cI+\\sum_j\\ell_j\\widehat z_j+\\tfrac14\\sum_{j,k}G_{jk}(\\widehat z_j\\widehat z_k+\\widehat z_k\\widehat z_j). $$\nFor each $0<\\epsilon\\le1$, assume a densely defined self-adjoint operator $H_{\\epsilon,h}$ on $L^2(\\mathbb R^d)$ extends $H_{\\epsilon,h}^0$ and $\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^d)$ is a core for it. Let $U_{\\epsilon,h}(t)$ be the strongly continuous unitary group with $U_{\\epsilon,h}(0)=I$, preserving $D(H_{\\epsilon,h})$ and satisfying\n$$ i\\,\\partial_tU_{\\epsilon,h}(t)y=\\epsilon^{-1}H_{\\epsilon,h}U_{\\epsilon,h}(t)y\\qquad(y\\in D(H_{\\epsilon,h})). $$\nIts generator is $-iH_{\\epsilon,h}/\\epsilon$. The global Hamiltonian flow, defined by $\\dot z=J\\nabla h(z)=J(Gz+\\ell)$ and $\\Phi_0(z)=z$, is\n$$ \\Phi_t(z)=e^{tJG}z+\\int_0^t e^{(t-s)JG}J\\ell\\,ds. $$\nHere $e^{tJG}:=\\sum_{n=0}^\\infty t^n(JG)^n/n!$ is the matrix exponential.\nThen for every $a\\in\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^{2d})$ and every $t\\in\\mathbb R$,\n$$ U_{\\epsilon,h}(t)^*\\operatorname{Op}^W_\\epsilon(a)U_{\\epsilon,h}(t)=\\operatorname{Op}^W_\\epsilon(a\\circ\\Phi_t). $$\n\n",

          "statement": "Assume Countable Choice. Let $M$ be a compact oriented smooth surface with boundary. Its boundary is a finite union of embedded $C^2$ arcs with pairwise disjoint interiors; each arc is the image of an injective $C^2$ parametrization with nonzero derivative, including one-sided derivatives at endpoints. Let $r\\ge1$, $\\hbar>0$, and put $J_0=\\begin{pmatrix}0&I_r\\\\-I_r&0\\end{pmatrix}$. In grouped order $(q,p)$, write\n$$S=\\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\\\C&D\\end{pmatrix}\\in M_{2r}(\\mathbb R),\\qquad A,B,C,D\\in M_r(\\mathbb R),\\qquad S^TJ_0S=J_0,$$\nand assume its upper-right block $B$ is invertible. Define\n$$R_g:=(Q_1,\\ldots,Q_r,P_1,\\ldots,P_r)^T.$$\nFix a compact interval $I=[0,T]$ with $T>0$. For each $j\\in\\{1,2\\}$, let $K_j:I\\to M_{2r}(\\mathbb R)$ have Lebesgue-integrable entries in grouped order and satisfy $K_j(t)=K_j(t)^T$ for every $t$. Let $S_j:I\\to M_{2r}(\\mathbb R)$ be absolutely continuous with $S_j(0)=I_{2r}$, $\\dot S_j(t)=J_0K_j(t)S_j(t)$ almost everywhere, and $S_j(T)=S$. Define the real symmetrically ordered quadratic operator on $\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^r)$ by\n$$H_{j,t}:=\\frac14\\sum_{a,b=1}^{2r}(K_j)_{ab}(t)((R_g)_a(R_g)_b+(R_g)_b(R_g)_a),$$\nwith no linear or scalar term. Assume $U_j:I\\to\\mathcal U(L^2(\\mathbb R^r))$ is a path of unitary Schwartz automorphisms with $U_j(0)=I$ such that, for each $f\\in\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^r)$, the path $t\\mapsto U_j(t)f$ is absolutely continuous in every Schwartz seminorm and satisfies\n$$i\\hbar\\,\\partial_tU_j(t)f=H_{j,t}U_j(t)f$$\nalmost everywhere. Here a unitary Schwartz automorphism is a unitary on $L^2$ whose restriction is a continuous linear bijection of $\\mathcal S$ with continuous inverse, and the Schwartz seminorms are $p_{\\alpha,\\beta}(f)=\\sup_x|x^\\alpha\\partial^\\beta f(x)|$ for multi-indices $\\alpha,\\beta$. Absolute continuity of each trajectory means the usual finite disjoint-interval condition for its increments in every seminorm. These hypotheses include piecewise-smooth Hamiltonian paths.\nThen\n$$U_2(T)=U_1(T)\\quad\\text{or}\\quad U_2(T)=-U_1(T).$$\nThe same conclusion holds after multiplying both propagators by a fixed\nnormalized quadratic propagator, provided the resulting endpoint lies in a\nchart with invertible upper-right block.",

          "id": "thm-nrqmx-finite-metaplectic-construction",
          "kind": "theorem",
          "domain": "mathematics",
          "title": "Finite symplectic implementation by quadratic generators",
          "statement": "Assume AC, $r\\ge1$, and $\\hbar>0$. Let $R=(Q_1,P_1,\\ldots,Q_r,P_r)^T$,\n$J=\\bigoplus_{j=1}^r\\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\\\-1&0\\end{pmatrix}$,\nand let $W(z)$ be the regular irreducible Weyl system of\n[[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. For every real\n$S\\in\\operatorname{Sp}(2r,\\mathbb R)$, there is a unitary $M_S$ on\n$L^2(\\mathbb R^r)$ such that\n$$M_S^*W(z)M_S=W(S^Tz)\\qquad(z\\in\\mathbb R^{2r});$$\nequivalently, $M_S^*RM_S=SR$ on the common transported Schwartz core.\nAny two such implementers differ by a scalar of modulus one. The same\nconstruction applies in every nonzero irreducible regular representation\nwith this finite phase space and fixed central parameter $\\hbar$, after the\nunitary equivalence of\n[[thm-nrqmx-finite-weyl-uniqueness-interface]].\n\nThere is also a connected topological group\n$\\operatorname{Mp}(2r,\\mathbb R)$ of normalized propagators of real\nhomogeneous quadratic Hamiltonians on this finite-mode Schrödinger space.\nHere a unitary Schwartz automorphism means a unitary on $L^2(\\mathbb R^r)$\nwhose restriction is a continuous linear bijection of the Schwartz space\n$\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^r)$ with continuous inverse. A normalized propagator is defined on a compact interval $[0,T]$ with $0<T<\\infty$. Its coefficient path $K:[0,T]\\to M_{2r}(\\mathbb R)$ has Lebesgue-integrable entries and is symmetric, $K(t)=K(t)^T$ for every $t$; an almost-everywhere symmetric integrable path is understood through a symmetric representative. In the displayed interleaved quadrature order put\n$$H_t=\\frac14\\sum_{a,b=1}^{2r}K_{ab}(t)(R_aR_b+R_bR_a)\\quad\\text{on }\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^r),$$\nwith no linear or scalar term. The path $U:[0,T]\\to\\mathcal U(L^2(\\mathbb R^r))$ consists of unitary Schwartz automorphisms, has $U(0)=I$, and for every $f\\in\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^r)$ its trajectory $U(t)f$ is absolutely continuous in each Schwartz seminorm $p_{\\alpha,\\beta}(g)=\\sup_x|x^\\alpha\\partial^\\beta g(x)|$ and satisfies $i\\hbar\\,\\partial_tU(t)f=H_tU(t)f$ almost everywhere. Absolute continuity in a seminorm means the finite disjoint-interval condition for the seminorms of the increments. The construction below proves existence, uniqueness and continuity of the inverse path in the same pointwise Schwartz topology. Precisely, $\\operatorname{Mp}(2r,\\mathbb R)$ is the set of all endpoint operators $U(T)$ for this integrable-coefficient class, over all such $T$ and $K$. Piecewise-smooth coefficient paths are included and yield the same endpoint set, as proved below; the definition does not restrict the admissible propagators to that subclass.\nGive $\\operatorname{Mp}$ the topology of pointwise convergence of $U$ and\n$U^{-1}$ on $\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^r)$ in its Schwartz topology; give\n$\\operatorname{Sp}(2r,\\mathbb R)$ its usual matrix topology.\nThe map\n$$\\pi:\\operatorname{Mp}(2r,\\mathbb R)\\longrightarrow \\operatorname{Sp}(2r,\\mathbb R),\\qquad M\\longmapsto S \\quad\\text{when }M^*W(z)M=W(S^Tz),$$\nis a two-fold covering homomorphism. Its two points over $S$ act by $M_S$\nand $-M_S$ when $M_S$ denotes either normalized lift; an arbitrary Weyl\nimplementer may differ from them by any scalar phase. This connected double\ncover and its unitary action are the metaplectic group and metaplectic\nrepresentation. All mode counts here are finite; no infinite-mode\nimplementation claim is part of the statement.\n\n",

          "title": "Finite Bogoliubov implementability",
          "statement": "Assume AC, $r\\ge1$, and the finite-mode Fock conventions of\nFinite-mode quadratures and symplectic data. Define the real permutation\nmatrix $\\Pi$ by\n$$\\Pi(x_1,y_1,\\ldots,x_r,y_r)^T=(x_1,\\ldots,x_r,y_1,\\ldots,y_r)^T,$$\nand, writing $Q=(Q_1,\\ldots,Q_r)^T$ and $P=(P_1,\\ldots,P_r)^T$, set\n$$R_g=\\Pi R=\\begin{pmatrix}Q\\\\P\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad J_0=\\Pi J\\Pi^T=\\begin{pmatrix}0&I_r\\\\-I_r&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad W_g(w)=W(\\Pi^Tw).$$\nThen the $a'_j$ satisfy $[a'_j,(a'_k)^*]=\\delta_{jk}I$ and\n$[a'_j,a'_k]=0$ on the finite Hermite core.           "statement": "Assume Countable Choice and let $d\\ge1$ be an integer. The form is Hermitian, densely\ndefined, and bounded below by $-v_0\\|u\\|_2^2$.\n\nFor $\\varepsilon_0>0$ define its shifted form norm by\n$$\\|u\\|_{q,v_0,\\varepsilon_0}^2=q_{A,V}[u]+(v_0+\\varepsilon_0)\\|u\\|_2^2.$$\nThe form is **closable** when every sequence $(u_n)\\subset\\mathscr D$ with\n$\\|u_n\\|_2\\to0$ and\n$\\|u_n-u_m\\|_{q,v_0,\\varepsilon_0}\\to0$ as $n,m\\to\\infty$ also satisfies\n$\\|u_n\\|_{q,v_0,\\varepsilon_0}\\to0$.           "statement": "Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, $m,\\hbar>0$, and real $q,B$\nwith $qB\\ne0$.           "statement": "Let $d\\ge1$. Regard $\\mathbb C^d$ as column vectors with the standard complex inner product\n$$\\langle x,y\\rangle:=\\sum_{j=1}^d x_j\\overline{y_j},$$\nlinear in the first argument, and induced norm $\\|x\\|=(\\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|^2)^{1/2}$. A matrix $A=(a_{ij})\\in M_d(\\mathbb C)$ acts by $(Ax)_i=\\sum_{j=1}^d a_{ij}x_j$, and its adjoint for this inner product is $A^*=\\overline A^{\\mathsf T}$.\n\nFor $A\\in M_d(\\mathbb C)$ and $z\\in\\mathbb C$, define the finite-dimensional matrix exponential by\n$$e^{zA}:=\\sum_{k=0}^{\\infty}\\frac{z^kA^k}{k!},\\qquad A^0=I_d.$$\nThe scalar exponential convention is $\\exp w=\\sum_{k\\ge0}w^k/k!$.\n\nEvery matrix $B=(b_{ij})\\in M_d(\\mathbb C)$ is bounded on $\\mathbb C^d$: since $|x_j|\\le\\|x\\|$, one has\n$$\\|Bx\\|^2\\le\\sum_{i=1}^d\\left(\\sum_{j=1}^d|b_{ij}|\\right)^2\\|x\\|^2.$$\nThus its operator norm is defined by the unit-ball supremum in the operator-norm definition listed in Definition references. For $B,C\\in M_d(\\mathbb C)$ and $\\|x\\|\\le1$, the operator-norm bound gives $\\|BCx\\|\\le\\|B\\|\\|Cx\\|\\le\\|B\\|\\|C\\|$; taking the supremum proves $\\|BC\\|\\le\\|B\\|\\|C\\|$. Homogeneity and the triangle inequality follow from the unit-ball supremum, and $\\|B\\|=0$ forces $Be_j=0$ for each coordinate vector $e_j$ (with entry $1$ at $j$ and $0$ elsewhere), hence $B=0$.           "title": "Wavefront and positive-frequency Hadamard data",
          "statement": "Let $M$ first be any Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary and $u\\in\\mathcal D'(M)$. Map a local covector $(x(p),\\xi)\\in T^*\\Omega$ to $(p,dx_p^T\\xi)\\in T^*M$. Define the global wavefront set by the union over all charts,\n$$ \\operatorname{WF}(u):=\\bigcup_{(U,x)}\\{(p,dx_p^T\\xi):(x(p),\\xi)\\in\\operatorname{WF}_{x(U)}(u_x)\\}\\subset T^*M\\setminus0, $$\nwhere the local sets are the local Fourier wavefront sets. Thus the global set is defined using all charts; equality of the chartwise descriptions on overlaps is a separate theorem. The Fourier convention is the displayed $2\\pi$ convention.\n\n\nLet $(M,g)$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented, time-oriented, globally hyperbolic smooth Lorentzian $n$-manifold without boundary, $n\\ge2$. Here $g$ is a smooth symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form on each tangent space with one negative and $n-1$ positive directions; in charts its signature is $(-,+,\\ldots,+)$. An orientation is a smooth choice of orientation in each tangent space. A time orientation selects one of the two components of $\\{v\\ne0:g(v,v)<0\\}$ as future. A tangent vector is causal when $g(v,v)\\le0$, and is future or past causal when it belongs to the closure of the selected future or past timelike cone. A future causal curve is a continuous map $c:I\\to M$, where $I\\subset\\mathbb R$ is an interval, which is piecewise $C^1$ on each compact subinterval, with finitely many pieces there and nonzero future causal tangent on each smooth piece. Past curves are defined with the opposite cone. Endpoint values, when included in $I$, are taken by continuity. Define $J^+(p)$ by including $p$ and all $q$ for which a future causal curve $c:[a,b]\\to M$, $a<b$, has $c(a)=p$, $c(b)=q$; put $J^-(p)=\\{q:p\\in J^+(q)\\}$. Here globally hyperbolic means strongly causal and every causal diamond $J^+(p)\\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; strongly causal means every point has arbitrarily small neighborhoods which each causal curve meets in a connected parameter interval. A nonzero cotangent vector is future or past causal, or future or past null, when its metric dual under $g^{-1}$ has the corresponding tangent property.\n\nHere is an explicit construction of the connection used below. A field configuration is any smooth real function $\\phi$; it is off shell because no field equation is imposed. The allowed local interactions are compactly supported finite polynomial functionals of $\\phi$ and finitely many coordinate derivatives, integrated against $d^4x$. The support of a functional $F$ is the closed set of points each of whose neighborhoods contains the support of a compactly supported variation that changes $F$ for some configuration.\n\nFor $\\Lambda\\in SO^+(1,3)$, require $\\Lambda^{\\mathsf T}\\eta\\Lambda=\\eta$, $\\det\\Lambda=1$, and preservation of the chosen future cone; $SO^+(1,3)$ denotes this identity component. The proper orthochronous Poincare group consists of $\\gamma=(a,\\Lambda)$ with $a\\in\\mathbb M$ and $\\Lambda\\in SO^+(1,3)$. It acts by $(\\gamma\\cdot\\phi)(x)=\\phi(\\Lambda^{-1}(x-a))$ and $(\\gamma\\cdot F)(\\phi)=F(\\gamma^{-1}\\cdot\\phi)$.\n\nFor a distribution on a coordinate chart, its wavefront set consists of the nonzero cotangent directions where every compact localization fails to have a rapidly decreasing Fourier transform in every conic neighborhood. Covectors are future or past causal when their metric-dual vectors are causal with the indicated time orientation; a nonzero causal covector has a nonzero time component. Write $\\Delta=\\{(x,x):x\\in\\mathbb M\\}$ and $N^*\\Delta=\\{(x,\\xi;x,-\\xi):\\xi\\ne0\\}$. Write $(x,\\xi)\\sim(y,\\zeta)$ when both covectors are nonzero null and cotangent to the same null straight line, with parallel transport carrying $\\xi$ to $\\zeta$. Precisely, for $x\\ne y$ there must be a future-directed nonconstant affinely parametrized null straight line $\\gamma$ and parameters $s,t$ in either order with $x=\\gamma(s)$, $y=\\gamma(t)$ and a real $\\lambda\\ne0$ such that $\\xi=\\lambda\\eta(\\dot\\gamma(s),\\cdot)$ and $\\zeta=\\lambda\\eta(\\dot\\gamma(t),\\cdot)$. When $x=y$, require $\\xi=\\zeta$ and allow every nonzero null covector. This relation is unsigned: the future first-covector condition below selects $\\lambda>0$, while the Feynman past branch selects $\\lambda<0$. A fixed free scalar input consists of $m\\ge0$, a two-point distribution $W$ satisfying\n$$P_xW=P_yW=0,\\qquad P=-\\eta^{ab}\\partial_a\\partial_b+m^2,$$\nand the positive-frequency null wavefront condition\n$$\\operatorname{WF}(W)=\\mathcal C^+:=\\{(x,\\xi;y,-\\eta):(x,\\xi)\\sim(y,\\eta),\\ \\xi\\text{ future null}\\}.$$\nFor a two-point distribution $U$, set $U^{\\mathsf T}(x,y)=U(y,x)$ and let $U^*$ be complex conjugation. Require $\\operatorname{sd}_0(h_F),\\operatorname{sd}_0(w)\\le2$ and\n$$\\operatorname{WF}(H_F)\\subseteq\\Gamma_F:=N^*\\Delta\\cup\\{(x,\\xi;y,-\\eta):x\\ne y,\\ (x,\\xi)\\sim(y,\\eta),\\ \\xi\\text{ future null if }x\\in J^+(y),\\ \\xi\\text{ past null if }x\\in J^-(y)\\}.$$\nThis is fixed conditional data: it does not claim existence of $W$ or $H_F$, and it does not define any singular restriction or product of $H_F$ on a diagonal.\n\nFor $r\\ge1$, $F^{(r)}(\\phi)$ denotes the distribution kernel on $\\mathbb M^r$ of the mixed variation in $r$ compactly supported smooth directions, and set $F^{(0)}(\\phi)=F(\\phi)$. For $F,G$ in this class, define\n$$F\\star_WG=\\sum_{r=0}^{\\min(\\deg F,\\deg G)}\\frac{\\hbar^r}{r!}\\left\\langle F^{(r)}(\\phi)\\otimes G^{(r)}(\\phi),W^{\\otimes r}\\right\\rangle,$$\nusing distribution products and pushforwards under the stated wavefront transversality conditions, with the $r=0$ pairing interpreted as the pointwise product $F(\\phi)G(\\phi)$. Here $\\hbar$ is a formal indeterminate, and Countable Choice is assumed for the supplier theorem defining these contractions.\n\nA scalar time-ordered system is a sequence of symmetric multilinear maps\n$$T_n:\\big(\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{loc}}^{\\mathrm{poly}}(\\mathbb M)\\big)^n\\longrightarrow \\mathcal F_{\\mu c}^{\\mathrm{poly}}(\\mathbb M)\\llbracket\\hbar\\rrbracket,\\qquad T_0=1,\\quad T_1=\\operatorname{id}.$$\nFor $I\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$ put $S_I=\\bigcup_{i\\in I}\\operatorname{supp}F_i$ and $F_I=(F_i)_{i\\in I}$. In the graph expansion of $T_n$, vertices are labeled by $1,\\ldots,n$ and an edge between distinct vertices contracts one derivative slot at each endpoint by $H_F$. No graph term uses a singular product at a diagonal before extension.\n\nFor $n\\ge2$, use relative coordinates $z_i=x_i-x_n$ ($1\\le i<n$), so the total diagonal corresponds to $0\\in\\mathbb R^{4(n-1)}$. The relative scaling degree $\\delta_\\Gamma$ of a numerical graph distribution is defined by the same positive-dilation rule above in this relative dimension. The scaling condition is imposed compatibly with integration by parts in the local functionals. First write every local density in its unique balanced-jet representative, in which the derivative variables at a degree-$r$ vertex are the relative combinations $q_a=p_a-r^{-1}\\sum_bp_b$. Any two extensions of a fixed punctured coefficient with upper bound $B_\\Gamma$ differ by derivatives $\\partial^\\beta\\delta_0$ of order $|\\beta|\\le\\lfloor B_\\Gamma-4(n-1)\\rfloor$ when $B_\\Gamma\\ge4(n-1)$, and agree when $B_\\Gamma<4(n-1)$. A differentiated coefficient is not required to retain the exact scaling degree of a punctured linear combination that vanishes: total differentiation may force a contact term at the diagonal.\n\nCovariance requires $T_n(\\gamma\\cdot F_1,\\ldots,\\gamma\\cdot F_n)=\\gamma\\cdot T_n(F_1,\\ldots,F_n)$ for each proper orthochronous Poincare transformation.           "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice and fix admissible scalar free data as defined by the local time-ordered product contract. Put $i_0=\\min S$ and use $(x_i-x_{i_0})_{i\\in S\\setminus\\{i_0\\}}$ as relative coordinates on the quotient by simultaneous translations.           "statement": "Assume Countable Choice as in [[def-countable-choice]]. On $H=\\mathbb C^2\\otimes\\mathbb C^2$, let\n$$\\psi=\\frac{|00\\rangle+|11\\rangle}{\\sqrt2},$$\nwhere $e_0=(1,0)$ and $e_1=(0,1)$ are the standard orthonormal basis of $\\mathbb C^2$, $j,a,b,c,d\\in\\{0,1\\}$, $|j\\rangle:=e_j$, and $|ab\\rangle:=e_a\\otimes e_b$. Give $H$ the inner product linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second determined by $\\langle e_a\\otimes e_b,e_c\\otimes e_d\\rangle=1$ if $a=c$ and $b=d$, and $0$ otherwise, extended by these sesquilinearity rules. Let $I_H$ be the identity on $H$. For either $K=H$ or $K=\\mathbb C^2$, write $\\mathcal B(K)$ for the bounded complex-linear maps $K\\to K$, with boundedness measured by the induced norm. Define the initial vector functional $\\omega:\\mathcal B(H)\\to\\mathbb C$ by $\\omega(C):=\\langle C\\psi,\\psi\\rangle$. For $j\\in\\{0,1\\}$ let $P_jx:=\\langle x,e_j\\rangle e_j$ for $x\\in\\mathbb C^2$; Alice uses the local projections\n$$M_0=P_0\\otimes I_2,\\qquad M_1=P_1\\otimes I_2,$$\nwhere $I_2$ is the identity on $\\mathbb C^2$. Bob's observable is $Z_B=I_2\\otimes Z$, with $Z$ the linear operator determined by $Z|0\\rangle=|0\\rangle$ and\n$Z|1\\rangle=-|1\\rangle$. Define the branch weight $p_j:=\\|M_j\\psi\\|^2$ and,\nwhen $p_j>0$, the normalized branch vector\n$\\psi_j:=M_j\\psi/\\sqrt{p_j}$. Each branch weight is $1/2$; conditional on\nbranch $0$ Bob's $Z_B$ expectation $\\omega_j(Z_B):=\\langle Z_B\\psi_j,\\psi_j\\rangle$ is $+1$, and conditional on branch $1$ it is $-1$.           "title": "Finite-quiver Hall spectrum generators",
          "statement": "Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite acyclic quiver, where $Q_0,Q_1$ are finite
sets and $s,t:Q_1\to Q_0$ are the source and target maps. Let $k=\mathbb F_q$
with $q>1$, and assign to each vertex $i\in Q_0$ a charge
$z_i\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$. A
finite-dimensional representation $M$ assigns a finite-dimensional
$k$-vector space $M_i$ to each vertex and a linear map
$M_a:M_{s(a)}\to M_{t(a)}$ to each arrow; its dimension vector is
$\mathbf d(M)=(\dim_k M_i)_{i\in Q_0}$. Put
$Z(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i z_i$ and, for nonzero
$\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$, put
$\phi_Z(\mathbf d)=\arg Z(\mathbf d)/\pi$ using the principal argument. For
$M\ne0$, set $\phi_Z(M)=\phi_Z(\mathbf d(M))$. Call $M$
$Z$-semistable when every nonzero subrepresentation has phase at most
$\phi_Z(M)$. Include the zero representation as semistable with no assigned
phase.

Use the small finitary abelian skeleton of these representations. Its Hall
algebra has basis $\delta_M$ indexed by isomorphism classes, and the
subobject-first convention is
$(f\star g)(L)=\sum_{U\subseteq L}f(U)g(L/U)$, with distinct embedded
subobjects counted separately. Its dimension completion is the product of
the finite-dimensional homogeneous components. For integer dimension
vectors define the bilinear Euler form and its skew-symmetrization by
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,\qquad \langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d).$$

For a phase $\phi$, let
$$S_Z(\phi)=\delta_0+\sum_{\substack{[M]\ne[0]\\M\ Z\text{-semistable}\\\phi_Z(M)=\phi}}\delta_M,$$
where $\delta_M$ is the characteristic function of the isomorphism class
$[M]$ and $\delta_0$ is the Hall unit. The Euler and skew integrations are
the continuous maps
$$I(f)=\sum_{[M]}\frac{f(M)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|}X^{\mathbf d(M)},\qquad J(f)=\sum_{[M]}t^{\chi_Q(\mathbf d(M),\mathbf d(M))}\frac{f(M)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|}x^{\mathbf d(M)},\qquad t=\sqrt q>0,$$
as proved for this finite-field category by the Euler and skew integration
theorem. Their completed targets have bases $X^{\mathbf d}$ and
$x^{\mathbf d}$ and products
$$X^{\mathbf d}X^{\mathbf e}=q^{-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d)}X^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e},\qquad x^{\mathbf d}*x^{\mathbf e}=t^{-\langle\mathbf e,\mathbf d\rangle}x^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}.$$

Write $\Phi_Z=\{\phi_Z(\mathbf e):\mathbf e\in\mathbb N^{Q_0},\
\mathbf e\ne0\}$ and order its elements decreasingly. Define the Euler and
skew Hall spectrum generators by
$$P_Z^{E}:=\prod_{\phi\in\Phi_Z}^{\searrow} I(S_Z(\phi)),\qquad P_Z^{\mathrm{sk}}:=\mathop{*}_{\phi\in\Phi_Z}^{\searrow}J(S_Z(\phi)).$$
In each product the largest phase is the leftmost factor and multiplication
is in the corresponding completed torus. In any fixed total-dimension degree
$D$, only dimension vectors with $\sum_i d_i\le D$ and their finitely many
phases can contribute. Thus these are degreewise formal products in the
specified completion; no analytic convergence is asserted.

These generators describe the Euler or skew integration of finite-field
semistable representation groupoids. Calling such data protected BPS indices,
dimensions of physical state spaces, or spectra of a four-dimensional
supersymmetric model is an additional dictionary, not part of this

          "statement": "Fix a finite nonempty set of states $E$, equipped with the discrete sigma-algebra $\\mathcal P(E)$ consisting of all subsets of $E$, and a finite time horizon $T\\ge0$. Thus each $X_t$ is a random element of this measurable state space. Its paths are constant between successive jump times and take the new state at a jump time (right-continuity); path events use the sigma-algebra generated by the coordinate maps $X_t$. The Markov property here means that, conditional on the history through time $s$, the law of the future path depends on that history only through $(s,X_s)$. For each pair of distinct states $x,y\\in E$, its transition rate $\\kappa_{xy}:[0,T]\\to[0,\\infty)$ is a bounded continuous function. Write\n\n$$\\lambda_x(t):=\\sum_{y\\in E,\\ y\\ne x}\\kappa_{xy}(t).$$\n\nAll time integrals without a displayed measure below are oriented Riemann integrals. When a continuous integrand is used as a Lebesgue density, its Lebesgue and Riemann integrals agree by the bounded Riemann-integral comparison theorem. The first-jump rate convention is the following. A time-homogeneous process is the special case in which every $\\kappa_{xy}(t)$ is constant.           "physical_scope": null,
          "statement": "Assume Countable Choice. All inner products are linear in their first\nargument. If $H$ is a complex Hilbert space, its **conjugate Hilbert space**\n$\\overline H$ consists of symbols $\\overline x$ for $x\\in H$, with\n$\\overline x+\\overline y=\\overline{x+y}$,\n$a\\,\\overline x=\\overline{\\overline a\\,x}$ for $a\\in\\mathbb C$, and\n$$\\langle\\overline x,\\overline y\\rangle_{\\overline H} :=\\overline{\\langle x,y\\rangle_H}.$$\nThe canonical map $c_H:H\\to\\overline H$, $c_Hx=\\overline x$, is a\nconjugate-linear surjective isometry.\n\nFor complex Hilbert spaces $H_1,H_2$, a linear operator $A$ is a linear map\n$A:D(A)\\to H_2$ on a linear domain $D(A)\\subseteq H_1$. Its graph is\n$\\Gamma(A)=\\{(x,Ax):x\\in D(A)\\}\\subseteq H_1\\oplus H_2$, with the direct-sum\nHilbert norm. It is densely defined when $D(A)$ is dense in $H_1$, and closed\nwhen $\\Gamma(A)$ is closed.\n\nFor a densely defined linear operator $A:D(A)\\subseteq H_1\\to H_2$, define\n$D(A^*)$ to consist of those $y\\in H_2$ for which\n$x\\mapsto\\langle Ax,y\\rangle_{H_2}$ is bounded on $D(A)$ in the $H_1$ norm.\nThe bounded functional extends uniquely to $H_1$; its Riesz vector\n$A^*y\\in H_1$ is specified by\n$$\\langle Ax,y\\rangle_{H_2}=\\langle x,A^*y\\rangle_{H_1} \\qquad(x\\in D(A)).$$\nThis defines the linear adjoint $A^*:D(A^*)\\subseteq H_2\\to H_1$.\n\nAn operator $S:D(S)\\subseteq H\\to H$ is **antilinear** when\n$S(ax+by)=\\overline a\\,Sx+\\overline b\\,Sy$. Its associated linear operator\n$\\widetilde S:D(\\widetilde S)\\subseteq\\overline H\\to H$ is\n$D(\\widetilde S)=c_H(D(S))$ and\n$\\widetilde S(\\overline x)=Sx$. For densely defined antilinear $S$, define\n$$S^*:=c_H^{-1}\\widetilde S^*,$$\non the domain $D(S^*)=D(\\widetilde S^*)$.           "statement": "Use the mathematical assumptions of the supplied chiral channel, including Countable Choice: every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Adopt SI units. $$\kappa_{\rm geom}:=\frac{1}{2r_s}=\frac{c^2}{4GM},\qquad k:=c\kappa_{\rm geom}=\frac{c^3}{4GM}>0.$$

Adopt one real, linear, massless, minimally coupled scalar field on $(\mathcal M,g)$. $$\operatorname{supp}(G_{\rm ret}f)\subseteq J^+(\operatorname{supp}f),\qquad\operatorname{supp}(G_{\rm adv}f)\subseteq J^-(\operatorname{supp}f),$$
where $J^\pm(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^\pm(p)$. With the positive metric density $d{\rm vol}_g=|\det(g_{ab})|^{1/2}|dx^0dx^1dx^2dx^3|$, fix the advanced-minus-retarded convention

$\mathcal L_{\operatorname{Ric}^2}(q):=\operatorname{Ric}_{cd}[q]\operatorname{Ric}^{cd}[q]\,d\mathrm{vol}_q$.

$$\delta I_{R^2}[g;h]:=\int_M\left.\partial_\epsilon\mathcal L_{R^2}(g_\epsilon)\right|_0,\qquad \delta I_{\operatorname{Ric}^2}[g;h]:=\int_M\left.\partial_\epsilon\mathcal L_{\operatorname{Ric}^2}(g_\epsilon)\right|_0.$$

background coefficients, of $h^{ab}$ and its coordinate derivatives through
